final_candidates.decision_summary: K119 is the catalytic lysine forming the internal PLP aldimine; its removal abolishes PLP-dependent catalysis in CBS.
C52 is a heme axial ligand; disrupting heme coordination strongly impairs CBS activity and stability.
H65 is the second heme-coordinating residue; mutating it destabilizes the heme environment and markedly reduces enzyme activity.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 are anchored by well-characterized essential residues; no new evidence is available to improve ranking.

history.rationale: Lys119 is the conserved PLP-Schiff-base (internal aldimine) anchor of CBS; removing the lysine abolishes cofactor binding and catalysis. This is a classic knockout mutation in PLP enzymes.
K119 is the well-established catalytic lysine forming the internal PLP aldimine; its mutation abolishes PLP binding/catalysis in CBS.
Cys52 is the heme axial ligand in CBS; its removal disrupts heme coordination and heme-dependent catalytic regulation. Strongly expected to impair or abolish activity.
C52 is a heme axial ligand in CBS; disrupting heme coordination strongly impairs enzyme activity and stability.
His65 is the second heme axial ligand; mutation destabilizes heme binding and active-site geometry. Expected severe loss of function.
H65 is the second heme-coordinating residue; mutating it destabilizes the heme environment and reduces activity.
Tyr223 is a conserved active-site residue implicated in substrate binding/orientation in the CBS catalytic domain. Its removal likely eliminates activity while keeping the fold largely intact.
Y223 is a conserved active-site residue involved in substrate positioning in the PLP pocket; mutation disrupts catalysis.
Arg224 is a highly conserved active-site residue adjacent to Tyr223, likely involved in substrate carboxylate recognition. Substitution with Ala should abolish substrate binding.
R224 neighbors the active site and contributes to substrate binding; alanine substitution should markedly reduce activity.
Arg266 corresponds to a well-known disease-associated site (R266 region) in CBS critical for catalytic activity; loss-of-function substitutions here are documented in homocystinuria.
